item.title: Why Bengals-Steelers is the biggest game at Paycor Stadium in years
item.description: Paycor Stadium hasn't seen a game like this coming weekend's Cincinnati Bengals-Pittsburgh Steelers AFC North showdown in quite some time. Pretty much every NFL game is "big" and important to some degree, but over the last three years, "big" in Cincinnati has taken the shape of the Bengals dropping their most-anticipated contests. Or they're fighting to climb back into the AFC playoff picture after a slow start. On Sunday, Nov. 16, the Bengals host the Steelers in what could be one of the most-anticipated games in Paycor Stadium history: A Week 10, Sunday Night Football , primetime affair between two 6-2 rivals with first place in the AFC North on the line. Suffice it to say games of this magnitude have been rare during the Cincinnati's three-season playoff drought. "This is as big of a game as we've had here for a while," Burrow said. "We lost to them early in the season. So number one, with the standings at the end of the year, you want that to be split. And number two, for first place outright. And so, like you said, huge game." The Steelers on Sept. 27 narrowly defeated the Bengals at Acrisure Stadium, 30-27, and forced a turnover on Cincinnati's final drive to avoid overtime, or worse. When's the last time the Bengals hosted a game of this relative magnitude at Paycor Stadium? Let's see. Does last season's Nov. 2 loss to the Chicago Bears meet that standard? The Bengals were 3-5 entering the game and 3-6 afterward. Most of the games after that point became about draft order. How about the 2024 season? In Week 17 that year, Cincinnati beat the Denver Broncos in overtime. But the win only brought the late-charging Bengals back to .500 at 8-8. They finished the year at 9-8 but were always a longshot to reach the postseason after a slow start to the season. Realistically, you're reaching back to the 2022 season to find anything comparable to the next edition of Bengals-Steelers. The teams' second meeting of 2026 has several characteristics that could make it a classic, too. There's the Aaron Rodgers-versus-Burrow quarterback matchup, to the primetime TV time slot, to the weather as some forecasts call for temperatures to drop below 40F as the game progresses. Burrow contended one win wouldn't decide the outcome of the AFC North, but breaking the Bengals-Steelers deadlock atop the division could actually be very determinative. Looking beyond this game, Cincinnati has just three games remaining against teams that currently have a winning record (two games against the Cleveland Browns (5-4), one against Kansas City Chiefs (6-2). The Steelers have two games against winning teams left on the schedule following their trip to Cincinnati (Denver Broncos (7-2), Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2). That being said, neither team can afford to take anyone likely, including the teams with losing records. The winless Tennessee Titans took Cincinnati to overtime on Nov. 1, which wasn't expected by many. The Steelers also have their entire season series against the Rave

item.title: DUU-VALL aboard! Jaguars players visit USS Carney to talk shared experience of being on ‘destroyers’
item.description: Three Jacksonville Jaguars players took time between football games to tour the USS Carney, a destroyer based at Naval Station Mayport. Tight ends Brenton Strange and Nate Boerkircher and Safety Rayuan Lane III, who serves in the Marine Corps Reserves, made a visit Tuesday - a day before Veterans Day. “Lots of happy sailors walked away with selfies and autographs,” a post on the Facebook page of Naval Station Mayport read. “What a treat leading up to Veterans Day!” The USS Carney is a guided-missile destroyer that was involved in 2023-2024 in combat-intensive U.S. Navy deployments in the Middle East and Eastern Mediterranean Sea. item.title: BYU vs Montana State Preview: Cougs Host Big Sky Favorites
item.description: PROVO, UT - NOVEMBER 6: Bruce Branch III #3 of the Brigham Young Cougars drives against Cahmai Crosby #2 of the Omaha Mavericks during the second half of their game at the Marriott Center on November 6, 2026 in Provo, Utah. item.title: Ja’Marr Chase says 2026 Bengals are better than 2021 Super Bowl team
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals superstar wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase has done a lot of winning in his football career and has been a part of many talented teams at different levels. From playing in the LHSAA Division I state championship game his sophomore season, to winning the NCAA National Championship in 2019 to going to the Super Bowl in 2021, he’s been on fantastic teams. He says the 2026 Bengals are the best. When Chase was asked if the 6-2 Bengals are the best Bengals team he’s played for, he said yes, and it’s not particularly close. “I would say, by far [this team is the best Bengals team I’ve played on],” he told Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer on Tuesday . “I know we went to the Super Bowl. We had a good run with those guys. This is another great group we have… Honestly, I think the whole team is one unit.” The Bengals’ improbable Super Bowl run following the 2021 season, and their narrow loss in the AFC Championship game the following season, were their last two playoff appearances. After three straight seasons of no playoff football, and a roster turnover on the defensive side of the ball, the Bengals are hoping to get back to the postseason once the 2026 regular season comes to an end. Burrow and the offense have put up staggering numbers over the last three weeks. If that trend continues, the sky’s the limit. What do you think? Are the 2026 Bengals better than the 2021 squad?

item.title: Maryland volleyball outmatched in straight-set loss to No. 10 Penn State
item.description: The University of Maryland Volleyball Team defeated Princeton University 3-0 at the XFINITY Center on September 12, 2026. | Jessie Reider/Testudo Times Maryland volleyball nearly matched No. 10 Penn State’s kill total in the second set, ending the frame a mere two kills behind. But the Nittany Lions created separation through the Terps’ self-inflicted mistakes. Despite playing solid volleyball centered around setter Sara Toth, Maryland ultimately closed the door on itself with eight attack errors in the set. With Penn State ahead 8-6, Emmi Sellman took the service line and immediately drilled an ace. On her next serve, Sydney Bryant rose up and sailed the ball wide. Bryant swung a mishit on the following play as well. That sequence was part of the Nittany Lions’ four-point run. While the Terps clawed back in the set, they couldn’t overtake Penn State. Maryland recorded 16 attack errors and eight reception errors in the match, finishing with a .167 hitting percentage in Wednesday’s 3-0 loss against Penn State. The defeat marked the Terps’ last home match of the season. “Honestly, I thought they were just better at serve and pass,” head coach Adam Hughes said. “They did a really good job from the endline, and that was one of the matchup things we were concerned with.” Still fighting for a spot in the Big Ten tournament, Maryland will travel to Rutgers and Ohio State hoping to pull off two gritty wins to fulfill Hughes’ preseason goals of a tournament spot. “The goal being this season was to get back to .500, to get to the Big Ten tournament, and to stay at the Big Ten tournament for a little bit,” Hughes said. “We are now playing in the last week of the season and still have all of our goals in front of us.” The Terps got off to a slow start, conceding the first five points without an answer. Brooklynne Brass slammed a ball to kickstart a surge of energy — the beginning of a 5-1 run that closed Penn State’s early deficit. Maryland’s front row showed flashes of excellence. Occasional hammers startled Penn State’s defense, while routine duo blocks allowed for a close mid-set game despite Maryland trailing in kills. With the game starting to get out of hand, Hughes called a timeout down 19-14. Bryant recorded a kill immediately after the break, but it was downhill from there. The Nittany Lions ran away with the first set, 25-17. Ava Brown earned Maryland the opening point of the second set. Penn State’s Kennedy Martin responded, though, and her team followed suit by going on a brief spurt to open up a small cushion. In the midst of the Lions’ streak, Toth notched a kill with a clever dump. Two straight Terps points followed Toth’s creative play, but the Nittany Lions responded with four uncontested points. Right as the set seemed to spiral out of control for the Terps, Bryant logged a kill, and Brown checked in and recorded two consecutive kills of her own. item.title: 2026 CIAC girls field hockey Class L tournament first round is complete. What you need to know
item.description: Darien's Guiliana Franchetti (9) runs the ball up field during their game against Fairfield Ludlowe in the FCIAC Field Hockey Championships Saturday, November 7, 2026 at Greenwich High School. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) The first round of the Class L CIAC field hockey tournaments was held Wednesday. Class M and S will play their quarterfinals Thursday. Here is the full schedule and scoreboard for the tournaments. Here's what you need to know: Blue Wave roll on Darien, the No. 1 team in Class L, beat No. 16 NFA 10-0 in the first round, extending a streak going back over two decades. The last time Darien lost in the first round of a CIAC tournament was in 2003 when it was defeated in the Class S tournament by Granby Memorial. The Blue Wave also lost in the 2002 first round after failing to even qualify for the tournaments in 2000 and 2001. The program shifted in 2000 when Mo Minicus was hired as head coach coming off a stint as the head coach at Bowdoin College. Minicus took over the program in 2000, made her first CIAC tournament in 2002, was named CHSCA Coach of the Year in 2003, led the Blue Wave to the Class M championship game in 2004, and won her first championship in 2007. Since then, the Blue Wave have appeared in 15 finals, winning 10 titles, including last year's Class L crown. In that span, they have lost in the semifinals four times and the quarterfinals just twice, in 2005 and 2015. They have reached the semifinals every season since 2016. Darien has not conceded a goal in the first round of any Class L tournament since 2018 when it beat New Canaan 3-2. The Blue Wave have now not allowed a goal in five straight tournament games going back to last season. Minicus, who won her 500th career game in the FCIAC quarterfinals against Ridgefield, has twice been the CHSCA Coach of the year and was named the NFHCA National Coach of the Year in 2010. Prior to her arrival, Darien had appeared in three CIAC finals from 1981-84, winning two titles. Darien did not reach a championship game from 1984-2004. Darien will face No. 9 Greenwich in the quarterfinals either Friday or Saturday FCIAC rules Seven of the final eight teams in Class L are from the FCIAC. The only team to break through was No. 7 Hall from the CCC, which beat No. 10 Farmington 1-0 in double overtime to advance to face No. 2 Staples in the quarterfinals. The FCIAC also had seven of eight quarterfinalists a year ago in Class L. A team from the FCIAC has won the last 12 Class L championships, including Darien beating Staples last season. Glastonbury and Darien were co-champions in 2014. The last time an FCIAC team didn't win a CIAC title was in 2002. Since 2004, an FCIAC team has won 18 Class L tournaments, including the 2016 tournament when Darien and Staples were co-champions. item.title: Vintage James Harden leads Cavs in 115-107 win over Knicks
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 11: James Harden #1 of the Milwaukee Bucks looks on against the New York Knicks during their game at Madison Square Garden on November 11, 2026 in New York City. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Cavaliers finally got a win over the New York Knicks after five straight losses dating back to last year’s Eastern Conference Finals. That felt good. James Harden, who has been a lightning rod for criticism, put together the best half of basketball he’s played this season. Harden scored 17 points on 3-for-5 three-point shooting in the first half, surpassing his season average of 15 points per game in just the opening quarters. The second half was more of the same from Harden, who finished with a season-high 32 points. His isolation scoring kept them from falling victim to any dry spells against New York’s defense. The Cavs have needed this type of production from their point guard. Harden’s slow start hasn’t been the only issue for this team — but it was one of the non-negotiables that would need to be addressed if the Cavs were ever going to get back on track. This was an encouraging step in the right direction for the 37-year-old star. Rookie Meleek Thomas gave quality minutes off the bench. Thomas found a rhythym early in the second quarter, snaking around pick-and-rolls and burying fall-away jumpers. His smooth shooting and defensive intensity have put Thomas ahead of schedule in his development. Thomas wasn’t the only young guard who impressed tonight. Tyrese Proctor continues to take steps forward in his sophomore season, scoring 15 points on 6-of-12 shooting. He’s a steady shooter who fights hard on defense and played a key role in Cleveland’s best runs tonight. Both Thomas and Proctor made big plays in the fourth quarter by feeding off of Donovan Mitchell’s gravity. The Knicks began trapping Mitchell aggressively, and it was Proctor and Thomas who served as release valves for this critical stretch of the game. The Knicks were led in scoring by Jalen Brunson with 27 points. Karl-Anthony Towns chipped in with 21 points while Deuce McBride added 19 points off the bench. New York’s off-ball movement is something the Cavs still struggle with. They conceded a handful of wide-open layups as a result of this. But Cleveland’s overall effort and connectivity were much higher than they had been in either of their last two games. Donovan Mitchell helped close the game by showing patience against pressure. He accepted New York’s double teams in the fourth quarter and got the ball out of his hands to allow his teammates to play with an advantage. item.title: Texas' Colin Simmons, Cam Coleman expected to play vs. LSU
item.description: Colin Simmons saw limited snaps last week at Missouri but was not on the SEC availability report for Texas' game at LSU on Saturday. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) AUSTIN - Texas is growing closer to returning to near full strength as edge rusher Colin Simmons and wide receiver Cam Coleman were not on the SEC availability report Wednesday night and are expected to play against LSU on Saturday night. Although defensive tackle Hero Kanu was listed as questionable with a shoulder injury, Simmons and Coleman's returns would give the Longhorns a huge lift after the nation's sack leader missed two games and was limited to 18 snaps against Missouri last week and Coleman sat out the the game against the Tigers. Simmons has been out with a high ankle sprain, and Coleman hurt a shoulder against Mississippi State . Tight end Nick Townsend was ruled out for Saturday's game along with running back Hollywood Smothers and offensive tackle Trevor Goosby, who are out for the season. LSU's All-SEC linebacker Whit Weeks is listed at questionable while right tackle Weston Davis is probable for Saturday. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. item.title: How Nia Hislop found her voice as a UMass women's soccer leader
item.description: NOTE : UMass journalism students teamed up with MassLive to take readers inside the UMass women’s soccer program, highlighting the players, coaches and stories that make the Minutewomen special. Through a series of features, students explore the people and perseverance behind a team that has its sights set on a successful postseason run. UMass heads into the MAC semifinals Tuesday, Nov. 10, looking to take another step toward a conference championship. In 1999, Shaka Hislop made his debut for Trinidad and Tobago’s men’s national soccer team at Hasely Crawford Stadium in Port of Spain. Seven years later, he helped the country reach its first World Cup. On April 17, 2026, nearly three decades after his own debut, Hislop watched his daughter take the same field, wearing the colors of Trinidad and Tobago for the first time. For Nia Hislop, a UMass women’s soccer captain, it was more than a national team debut. It was a chance to follow in her father’s footsteps, represent her family’s homeland and begin a new chapter in a journey that had already taken plenty of twists. “The first time I touched the ball, or I did something good, the stadium was so loud,” Nia Hislop said. “I was like, oh my God, this is legit.” As she stepped onto the moss-green field as a 62nd-minute substitute, she scanned the crowd for her family amid an ocean of passionate Trinidadian supporters. A section of roughly 30 friends and family members cheered, wearing shirts with “Hislop” printed across the back. Her mother, Desha, broke into tears of joy. Her father, Shaka, sat beside her and tried to take in the moment without breaking down himself. “It invoked so many emotions in me,” Shaka said. “Seeing [Nia], she came off the bench to come on and play. Just as a dad ... I held it together. But above all, I wanted that moment to be about her and her journey in this game and everything that it meant to her through the years.” UMass captain Nia Hislop (32) dribbles the ball during action earlier this season at Rudd Field in Amherst. Photo by Trang Nguyen At home, her siblings exchanged excited texts, sharing pictures of their sister on the television screen. In Amherst, Massachusetts, her college teammates screamed at the television, recording their reactions to send to Nia after the match. UMass women’s soccer coach Jason Dowiak also watched the moment unfold from his couch at home. “I was taking videos of it and sending it to my friends, and I was like, ‘That’s my girl, that’s my girl,’” Dowiak said. Her national team debut marked a significant milestone in Nia’s return to the field after a season-ending hip injury forced her to miss the 2025 collegiate campaign. The injury sidelined her for her entire senior season and represented a low point in her career: her first major setback after years of success. item.title: Red Sox’s Craig Breslow Hints at ‘Sweeping’ Changes Inside Organization
item.description: With the Trade Deadline looming, a question of trust hangs over the Boston Red Sox and CBO Craig Breslow. Getty To say the Boston Red Sox dealt with the injury bug in 2026 would be an understatement. Star players such as outfielder Roman Anthony and ace Garrett Crochet spent significant time on the injured list with little to no communication between the organization and the general public. Especially with Anthony, even the team didn’t seem to fully understand the injury. Now, Craig Breslow has decided to add some accountability to the Red Sox. According to MassLive’s Christopher Smith, the organization is taking a longer look at its medical department and how it should best function moving forward. What Did Boston Red Sox CBO Craig Breslow Say? While Boston made the playoffs after a horrific start to the season that included firing manager Alex Cora, injuries and communication remained at the forefront of everyone’s mind. “We’re constantly assessing ‘what are we getting right, what are we getting wrong, what are the opportunities to improve,’” Breslow told Smith. “And I think it’s important to try and decouple — are we getting the diagnosis or the rehab wrong, or do we need to make sure that communication with our players, with our staff internally, with the media externally is tightened up? And so we’re going to evaluate all those things this offseason and definitely recognize where some of the criticism is coming from.​” Every team obviously deals with injuries throughout a major league season. However, to see a team so shorthanded and have no communication with the fans is disappointing. The Red Sox’ medical staff had several gaffes this season where the issue was misdiagnosed or was more of a problem than expected. Examples of Why There Needs to Be Change Reliever Garrett Whitlock underwent testing at the end of the season that found he was pitching on a fractured tibia. The Red Sox only diagnosed the injury after recurring leg pain forced more imaging. As for Boston’s ace, several setbacks kept Crochet sidelined from April 26 to Boston’s Wild Card series. But the most notable gaffe of all was Anthony’s injury. Interim manager Chad Tracy expected Anthony to be day-to-day with a wrist injury. That ailment would keep him out for over 100 games (until August 30) and forced him to miss postseason time. Boston cleared Anthony to play. However, he was dealing with pain throughout his return, making the decision questionable at best. While Breslow acknowledged that Anthony and Crochet will be ready for next season, these misdiagnoses altered Boston’s season permanently. “We’re going to take kind of a sweeping look at a number of our processes and make sure that we are diagnosing injuries the best we possibly can,” Breslow said. Breslow needs to make changes if Boston doesn’t want history to repeat itself. item.title: Trae Young shows off early chemistry with AJ Dybantsa on slick lob dunk
item.description: Mandatory Credit: David Richard-Imagn Images Trae Young shows off early chemistry with AJ Dybantsa on slick lob dunk appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Washington Wizards had to wait a bit for No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa to make his season debut following an early injury, but the talented rookie has already developed strong chemistry on the court with star point guard Trae Young. During the Wizards’ game against the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday evening, Trae Young dribbled the ball into the frontcourt and found AJ Dybantsa cutting along the baseline for a nice lob dunk. The play occurred late in the second quarter. Young rejected the screen by Anthony Davis and drove towards the paint where he saw Dybantsa getting behind the defense in position for a lob pass. TRAE YOUNG THROWS UP THE LOB FOR AJ DYBANTSA 🔥 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) pic.twitter.com/72KEZidRJ2 — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 12, 2026 As of publication, the Wizards and Pacers were tied at 77 heading into the fourth and final quarter. Dybantsa had nine points, two rebounds and one steal in 25 minutes while Young had 10 points, three rebounds, four assists and one steal in 24 minutes. Dybantsa was sidelined for the Wizards’ first four games due to an ankle injury. He did not make his debut until Oct. 28 in a loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers. He finished that game with 19 points, two rebounds and two assists in a little over 26 minutes of play. The former BYU star has appeared in seven games in his rookie season thus far, at a little over 32 minutes per game. He’s averaging 16.7 points, 6.1 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.1 steals with splits of 43.3 percent shooting from the field, 27.3 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 77.1 percent shooting from the free-throw line. The Wizards are currently 4-7 and looking to snap a four-game losing streak. item.title: LSU gymnastics inks top recruiting class, five defer for Olympics
item.description: On Wednesday, the LSU gymnastics team signed 10 recruits to the classes of 2027 and 2028 which formed the top recruiting class in the nation. Last year, LSU got commitments from nine gymnasts, a number which shocked most people considering the new roster limits. Those who’d been paying attention, as well as those who read my coverage, would know that the size would make sense once the class split. This signing day made that split clearer. In the class of 2027, LSU signed Myla Ruck, Jada Oliver, Kiari Sparks, Sage Bradford and Josie Lynch. These five will be part of the 2028 team. Five others announced that they’d be signing and also deferring their enrollment by a year to train for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Hezly Rivera joined the nine who committed in 2025 in signing with LSU, and Team USA hopefuls Tatum Drusch and Reese Esponda joined her in signing and deferring. As I speculated, Canadian elites Lia Redick and Zoé Cadrin are also deferring their enrollment to try and earn a spot on their country’s national team. Those five will join LSU for the 2029 season. LSU hasn’t finished looking for recruits in the 2028 recruiting class. On Saturday, they hosted American elite standouts Charleigh Bullock and Caroline Moreau, the latter of which seemed to really enjoy her time based on the three TikToks she made head coach Jay Clark do. LSU has room to add both without much issue right now.

item.title: Traded MN Twins Pitcher Wins Reliever of the Year
item.description: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect This season, the Minnesota Twins finished with a 77-85 record . They were largely sunk by a bullpen that couldn’t keep games together after their starter departed. Of course, that group was depleted at the trade deadline during the 2025 season. Tom Pohlad and Jeremy Zoll opted against rebuilding it during the offseason. It made sense to trade expiring relief assets from a team that ultimately finished with a 70-92 record . It didn’t make much sense to part out future assets for pennies on the dollar. That’s what the MN Twins did with hometown talent Louis Varland, though. Now, less than two years later, he’s won an award as the best reliever in the American League. Louis Varland finds new heights away from MN Twins A former 15th-round pick, Louis Varland found success in the Minnesota Twins bullpen. He finished with a 2.97 ERA in 2025, but it was dragged down by a 4.94 ERA with Toronto after he was sent to Canada . A year later, he posted a career-best 1.27 ERA. Louis Varland is the 2026 BBWAA American League Reliever of the Year! https://t.co/D7FfiSJtoh — MLB (@MLB) November 12, 2026 Related: Twins’ Star Catcher Plans to Decline QO; Now What? Varland reached a career-high 72 2/3 innings in 2025, and then outdid that number with 78 in 2026. What was more impressive, though, is that he took over the closer job from former teammate and new Twins pitcher Jeff Hoffman . That meant his innings this past season largely came in high-leverage spots. The Blue Jays used the former Division II Concordia St. Paul product to rack up 35 saves. He struck out 97 while walking just 23 and allowing only two home runs. After pushing his average fastball velocity to 98.1 mph in 2025, he reached new heights with a 98.8 mph average this season. A close vote for the AL Reliever of the Year award Voting for American League Reliever of the Year was incredibly close . Varland finished with 146 points and 16 first-place votes, while Cade Smith (Guardians) was second with 133 points and seven first-place votes. Bryan Baker (Rays) was third with 111 points, and Aroldis Chapman (Red Sox) and Josh Hader (Astros) also received votes. The award adds to a season in which he was named an All-Star for the first time as well. Still under team control through 2030, Varland remains a bargain and has made just shy of $2.3 million over the course of his career. He’ll be an integral part of the Toronto bullpen again in 2027, and there’s no reason to think he won’t still be among the game’s most dominant arms. Read more at Minnesota Sports Fan

(Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Seahawks got their trades wrapped up well before the trade deadline date of Nov. 10. Back on Oct, 27, general manager John Schneider sent a 2027 third round pick and a 2028 fifth round draft pick for guard Quentin Nelson; the first domino to fall in what ultimately became an Indianapolis Colts fire-sale that saw Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Josh Downs and Keenan Allen all get traded prior to Tuesday at 4pm ET. Even though the deadline has now passed, there are still areas within which to maneuver if Seattle are looking to make further upgrades to the offense. And one potential addition could end up being San Francisco 49ers wideout Brandon Aiyuk after some telling comments from his agent, Drew Rosenhaus on Tuesday. The main reason being the existing relationship between Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury, who was on the 49ers staff from 2019 – 2025: the entirety of Aiyuk’s time in the Bay Area. Brandon Aiyuk Likely to Join Team With Past Relationship – Agent Aside from noting that Aiyuk had already passed multiple physical examinations done by the team, Rosenhaus posited that the most likely way that the former All-Pro wideout would end up on a roster that intends to play him – the 49ers are expected to release him in the near future – is to find a link to someone who has an existing connection with him. Drew Rosenhaus on @PatMcAfeeShow : “I think that in all likelihood Brandon (Aiyuk) would probably sign with a team that knows him, somebody that has somehow been affiliated with him either in college or the #49ers . item.title: Knicks’ G League affiliate takes a chance on former lottery pick Rob Dillingham
item.description: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Knicks’ G League affiliate takes a chance on former lottery pick Rob Dillingham appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Rob Dillingham is hoping to return to the NBA after being waived by the Charlotte Hornets in September. Dillingham has yet to find a home in the league , playing for two teams—the Minnesota Timberwolves and the Chicago Bulls—in two seasons. He will have a chance to audition for the New York Knicks , as he is set to sign with the Westchester Knicks in the NBA G League , according to The Stein Line’s Jake Fischer. “Rob Dillingham is signing to the NBA G League, sources say, where the former lottery pick is expected to join the Westchester Knicks, depending on the waivers process,” wrote Fischer on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 21-year-old Dillingham was the No. 8 pick in the 2024 NBA Draft after a one-and-done stint at Kentucky. He, however, barely played in his rookie year with the Timberwolves, averaging 4.5 points and 2.0 assists per 10.5 minutes in 49 games. His situation did not change in his sophomore year. In February, he was traded to the Bulls, along with Leonard Miller and four second-round picks, in exchange for Ayo Dosunmu and Julian Philips. He had his moments with the Bulls, tallying 9.6 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 2.8 assists per 21.5 minutes in 30 games. Dillingham’s solid showing, however, was not enough to convince the front office to keep him. The Bulls traded him to the Hornets in exchange for Buddy Hield, but he was released. If everything goes well in the NBA G League, Dillingham could land with the Knicks. He could provide energy, speed, and quickness off the bench, although the defending champions are already stacked in the backcourt, with Jalen Brunson, Josh Hart, Landry Shamet, Miles McBride, Tyler Kolek, Jose Alvarado, and Jordan Clarkson. The Toronto Raptors considered acquiring Dillingham before going with Kevin McCullar Jr. Related: Jarrett Allen puts OG Anunoby on poster with clutch dunk Related: Knicks’ Mike Brown shouts out his Air Force veteran dad before Cavs clash

item.title: New Zealand vs. India 4th ODI prediction, lineups and Bay Oval pitch report — who will win?
item.description: New Zealand vs. India 4th ODI prediction, lineups and Bay Oval pitch report — who will win? originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Hamilton offered New Zealand a cruel sort of mercy. The rain turned up the day before the game and simply refused to leave. There was one thin gap in the clouds, enough for India to win the toss for the seventh time in eight on this tour and send the hosts in, and then the sky closed over again. Nobody got to bowl a ball. New Zealand had won 11 home bilateral ODI series on the spin, the second-longest run the format has seen, and it ended on a wet outfield. Now they trail 2-0 with two games to play, and the best they can manage is a share of the series. That means winning at Bay Oval on Friday, November 13 and again two days later. India will have a new voice in the huddle. Shubman Gill has played his last match of the tour as he turns to red-ball preparation, so Shreyas Iyer takes the armband. New Zealand vs. India prediction: who will win? Arshdeep Singh and Gurnoor Brar shared seven wickets in Auckland, and the chase of a reduced target was done with plenty of overs in hand. In Wellington, New Zealand were bowled out cheaply again, and India were ahead on the rain-adjusted par when the weather intervened. New Zealand's batters have not yet found a way to build an innings against this attack and have scored 185 and 134. Indian batters have also found the going difficult, but they have done enough to better their counterparts. The Cricket News Prediction : India to win. New Zealand vs. India predicted lineups, team news for 4th ODI Here's how we think both sides will line up in this game: New Zealand predicted lineup against India Will Young, Tim Seifert, Henry Nicholls, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Tom Latham (wk), Mitchell Santner (c), Nathan Smith, Kyle Jamieson, Kristian Clarke, Jacob Duffy India predicted lineup against New Zealand Rohit Sharma, Ishan Kishan, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer, KL Rahul (wk), Naman Dhir, Axar Patel, Anshul Kamboj, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar, Arshdeep Singh New Zealand vs. India pitch report, 4th ODI, Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui The numbers here lean towards chasing, with bowling first the slightly happier option over the 32 matches in the record. First innings scores average 235, so this is a surface where patience and a few middle-overs wickets usually count for more than fireworks. item.title: 9 Central Texas teams, 19 players to watch in the UIL high school football playoffs
item.description: Weiss Wolves linebacker Noah McPeak (0) listens during a huddle in the third quarter as the Wolves play the Lake Travis Cavaliers at the Pfield in Pflugerville, Sept. 4, 2026. Lake Travis won the game 38-21. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Central Texas high school football teams are perennial threats to make deep runs in the UIL playoffs . But who has the best chance in 2026? And what players should Austin-area fans be keeping an eye on? With the postseason getting underway Thursday - though most teams play Friday - the American-Statesman takes a look at teams and players to watch. MORE: Central Texas high school football primer for the UIL playoffs The teams range from Lake Travis to Thorndale in size and distance, and the players represent programs from East View to Hays. These are the teams that should play into at least the third round, and the players listed give their teams a chance to win any game. Here are nine teams and 19 players to watch from Central Texas in the UIL playoffs: Teams to watch Anderson The fact the Trojans are on this list, let alone in the postseason, tells one how far they've come. It's the first time in program history they've made the playoffs three years in a row. Quarterback Cove Darbyshire gets the headlines, but Anderson has talent all over its offense in running backs Nick Briggs and Kam'ron Hornsby and wideouts Jay Fullmer, Kyler Sharp and Gage Willis. Zach Cecalek, who has seven sacks, leads an underrated defense. Expect Anderson to still be alive Thanksgiving weekend in Class 5A Division I. Cedar Park The Timberwolves might be able to play the disrespect card. Despite being 10-0, they still probably don't get the attention they deserve statewide. David Cooper (2,243 yards, 20 TDs passing), Lucas Viloria (887 yards, 12 TDs rushing) and Brayden Jahns (1021 yards, 6 TDs receiving) pace a balanced offense, while Deshaun Stewart, CJ Rogers and Olujimi Aluko lead a talented defense. Cedar Ridge The Raiders are no longer a surprise. After going 9-1 and beating Lake Travis in the regular season, Cedar Ridge could make a playoff run. Defensive lineman Jeremiah Passmore, linebacker Ayden O'Brien Brown and defensive back Trent Bell would start for any team in Central Texas, and quarterback Dylan Snoga paces an electric offense. The Raiders have a tough first-round matchup against Dripping Springs, but if they get past that, they should have a rematch with Westlake in the Class 6A Division II regional finals. Hutto It's not a question of if the Hippos will be effective on offense, but how many points they'll score. The wideout trio of Jaiden Fields, Dylan Owens and Carson Fields is one of the best in the state, and quarterback Micah Antoun is a rising star. If Hutto comes together on defense, it will stick around in Class 6A Division I. Lake Travis The Cavs may be the most intriguing team in the Austin area. item.title: Luka Doncic sends bad message to Bucks with ridiculous trick shot
item.description: Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Luka Doncic sends bad message to Bucks with ridiculous trick shot appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Lakers visit the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday evening bringing a six-game win streak with them. And if Luka Doncic ’s pregame warmups are any indication, the Bucks are in for a long night with the Lakers in town. The master of trick shots, Luka Doncic calmly sank an incredible warmup shot prior to the Lakers’ game against the Bucks. The shot was caught on camera by Cameron Ezeir of CBS 58 News of Doncic launching a high-rainbow jumper from near the corner between the sideline and halfcourt. Casual from Luka 😳😳 pic.twitter.com/C7wHUcxqhr Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Cameron Ezeir (@camezeir) November 12, 2026 Doncic has been on an offensive tear to begin the 2026-27 season . He’s a frontrunner for the MVP Award and has led the Lakers to the top spot in the Western Conference standings. He’s presently leading the league in scoring at 39.3 points, while shooting 49.8 percent from the field, 40.7 percent from the 3-point line and 88.1 percent from the free-throw line. All of those shooting percentages are career-highs. The six-time All-Star has also been averaging 7.8 rebounds, 7.9 assists and 2.0 steals at a little over 36 minutes across 10 games played. He’s also leading the league in field goals made and attempted, 3-pointers made and attempted and free-throws made and attempted. Doncic is in his second full season with the Lakers after being traded by the Dallas Mavericks ahead of the 2024-25 trade deadline. He signed a contract extension with the organization in the 2025 offseason for three years and worth around $165 million. The Slovenian native is in his ninth season in the NBA and has solidified himself as the Lakers’ franchise player of the future. Related: Are Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes playing tonight? item.title: Keenan Allen provides critical update on beef with Mike Evans
item.description: Keenan Allen and Mike Evans resolve their differences. Any chance of hard feelings between Mike Evans and Keenan Allen has been squashed and thrown into the trash. A day after being traded to the 49ers, Allen met with members of the media for the first time with a large smile on his face and was asked about his previous rivalry with Evans. “We squashed it a long time ago. Fast than me… every day of the week but separation.. CHILD PLEASE!” Evans responded to Allen’s comment and called him out for tagging “the wrong Chris Godwin.” “Don’t be mad at us we ain’t make the rankings or care about em. item.description: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images Brewers star Jacob Misiorowski’s ‘awesome’ admission after winning Cy Young following World Series appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Milwaukee Brewers star Jacob Misiorowski has officially won the National League Cy Young Award. It comes as no surprise, as The Miz was the best pitcher in the NL throughout the 2026 campaign. In fact, he won the award via an anonymous vote, as the pitcher earned all 30 votes in the NL. The right-hander appeared on MLB Network to share how he was feeling after the announcement was made. “This is unreal,” Misiorowski said. “It’s amazing… It’s an honor to represent my city and my teammates. Just being in this situation is awesome.” It’s been a whirlwind season for Misiorowski. He kicked things off strong by earning his second All-Star selection in only his second MLB season. The Miz then played a crucial role in the Brewers’ World Series win . And now, following a stellar season that saw him pitch to a 1.80 ERA to go along with 252 strikeouts across 174.2 innings, Jacob Misiorowski is a Cy Young winner. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So, what has The Miz been doing since winning the World Series following his incredible campaign? “I actually got the chance a few days ago to hunt with my dad, so that was probably one of the big highlights,” Misiorowski said. “Went to a Chiefs game, so getting to live life just normally now, now that baseball’s over for the season.” The Brewers star was also asked about the people who helped him get to this moment. “Everyone here, my mom, my dad, my fiancé, her family, my agent all helped me get through this, and get to where I’m at today,” Misiorowski added. “It’s been awesome to have those people support me along the way.” It wouldn’t be surprising to see Jacob Misiorowski win more Cy Young awards throughout his big league career. item.title: Russian cloud Yandex says drone attacks on its datacenters caused data loss
item.description: Russian cloud operator Yandex has admitted to data loss after a drone attack on one of its datacenters. The attack, which Ukrainian press said was ordered by Kyiv, happened in early October and caused a fire and subsequent outage at Yandex’s ru-central1-b availability zone. Subsequent strikes targeted more Yandex datacenters and disrupted more of the company’s cloud and payment services. On Tuesday, Yandex posted an update on its recovery efforts, which it spun as something of a triumph because it restored over 97 percent of customer data. Of course that also means the company lost 2.84 percent of customer data, which it blamed on “critical hardware damage and a lack of backups on the platform.” It’s unclear if Yandex’s use of the phrase “on the platform” indicates it doesn’t keep backups of its own cloud, if whatever resilience techniques it employs don’t create multiple copies of customer data, or if clients didn’t protect their data. Whatever happened, Yandex has decided to enable backups by default for all VMs customers create in its cloud. That decision will mean customers will consume and pay for more Yandex resources, unless they opt out of the automated backups. Given that drones damaged three Yandex locations, and the war with Ukraine continues, users have good reasons to consider alternatives to its services. Indeed, Yandex’s announcement of its recovery efforts links to a page extolling the virtues of a hybrid cloud when devising data protection strategies. That page also mentions Yandex’s own Stackland product, which brings its stack on-prem, as an example of a hybrid approach. On Wednesday the company also launched a new availability zone named ru-central1-f. Yandex didn’t say where it’s located, other than to say it’s in “a new location.” Interestingly, Yandex has imposed quotas that limit the amount of resources users can access in the new availability zone and says it can’t yet handle traffic to private endpoints at the new facility. Many nations have imposed sanctions that restrict sales of technology products to Russia. It’s therefore unsurprising that Yandex might struggle to provision enough infrastructure to allow untrammeled access to a new availability zone. ®

item.title: Gowon’s memoirs: Nigeria owes Awolowo an eternal debt, by Olu Fasan
item.description: Last week, I started a discussion of General Yakubu Gowon’s multi-themed memoirs, My Life of Duty & Allegiance. My focus was on the book’s general tone, which I find unduly self-justificatory. In his attempts to defend his legacy, General Gowon presents himself as a saintly figure who did no wrong as a leader, whereas some introspection and nuanced reflection would have helped. That said, the book is a treasure trove of insightful details that enrich our historical narrative. This week, I will focus on one of such insights, namely, the quality of governance and public service ethos under General Gowon’s regime, with Chief Obafemi Awolowo singled out as the arrowhead of a remarkable governance approach that, if replicated today, would transform how Nigeria is governed and, thus, this country’s fortunes. As a political economist and policy practitioner who spent nearly 20 years advising the UK government on diverse policy areas, in addition to teaching public policy, I have professional and intellectual interests in how government is run. Thus, I was enthralled by General Gowon’s fascinating accounts of how the affairs of state were conducted under his administration, with the triumvirate of politicians (as ministers), civil servants (as technocrats), and universities and think-tanks (as sounding boards) driving policy formulation and implementation and setting standards of good and effective governance. Sitting atop the triumvirate was Chief Awolowo, an extraordinarily transformative leader! Indeed, if General Gowon’s memoirs can be said to have a hero, that hero is Chief Obafemi Awolowo, appointed by Gowon as the Vice Chairman of the Federal Executive Council, FEC, and Commissioner of Finance in his administration. In every reference to Chief Awolowo in the memoirs, General Gowon writes glowingly and superlatively about him. Gowon also gives credit to his colleagues in the Supreme Military Council, SMC, and the first-class mandarins who ran the civil service for his administration’s successes, especially its ability to prosecute a 30-month civil war “without endangering the national economy”. But he reserves his most generous praise for Chief Awolowo. Hear Gowon: “Chief Awolowo’s business acumen, political sagacity, economic wizardry and thorough man-management ability would later prove quite useful and helpful in ensuring that we kept our finances intact during and immediately after the civil war that broke out a few weeks after his appointment to the FEC.” He adds: “Without any argument, he made invaluable contributions.” Of course, Chief Awolowo’s reputation preceded him. As the premier of the Western Region, he performed so superbly that Harold Wilson, then British prime minister, described him as a “world-class leader”, who would make an outstanding President of America or Prime Minister of Britain. General Gowon himself referenced Chief Awolowo’s pedigree, saying that he appointed him as the Commissioner of Finance with concurrent responsib

item.title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 5063-5069 Rocks and Chips
item.description: Curiosity Navigation Curiosity Home Mission Overview Where is Curiosity? Mission Updates Science Overview Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Curiosity Raw Images Images Videos Audio Mosaics More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home 2 min read Curiosity Blog, Sols 5063-5069 Rocks and Chips NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity acquired this image of chip-shaped crystal forms using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI), located on the turret at the end of the rover’s robotic arm, on November 7, 2026, Sol 5067 of the Mars Science Laboratory Mission, at 14:07:35 UTC. NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS Written by William Farrand, Senior Research Scientist, Space Science Institute Earth planning date: Friday, Nov. 6, 2026 This week Curiosity has been completing its drill campaign at the “Nazca” drill hole. This is an area characterized by bedrock containing disk-shaped (or in a liberal interpretation, potato chip shaped … see linked image) crystal forms. A key objective has been to better characterize these chip-shaped features. Drill samples were delivered to the Sample Analysis for Mars (SAM) instrument. While the SAM analysis was on-going, Monday’s plan included a ChemCam LIBS observation of another crystal-form, “Ahi Veremos,” more Mastcam frames to fill out a mosaic of the Nazca near to mid-field, and environmental observations including a large dust devil survey, and horizon and atmospheric zenith movies. Wednesday’s plan included two targeted science blocks with a LIBS depth profile of the “Colca” crystal-form and LIBS of the “Bermejo ” target. A long distance Remote Micro-Imager (RMI) mosaic of rock clusters below the “Cordillera” ridge was also collected. Mastcam collected more frames of its Nazca mosaic, and more environmental observations were made. Friday’s planning was for three sols with three targeted science blocks and a drive away from the Nazca drill site. A MAHLI mosaic of the side of the block that hosts the Nazca drill hole was planned. It was also planned to use MAHLI’s nighttime white-light and ultraviolet LED lamps for nighttime imaging of the crystal-forms. Mars’ moon, Phobos, was eclipsing the Sun and imaging of that event was prioritized. ChemCam LIBS observations were planned for each sol including a cluster of crystal forms, a resistant layer in the side of the Nazca block and a dark float rock. A long distance RMI mosaic of dark lenses beneath a planar surface on the “Mishe Mokwa” ridge was to be made. Another round of environmental observation was also planned. Finally, Friday’s drive was to take the rover back towards its southerly trending route where Curiosity would continue its trek of exploration and discovery. item.title: The US built world’s greatest card system
item.description: By YVONNE-FAITH ELAIGWU The history of payments is, in many ways, the history of making value easier to move. We started at barter and are now at electronic transfers, with stablecoins suggesting that the next evolution is here. New payment methods rarely make their predecessors useless. Cash did not immediately eliminate barter. Cards did not eliminate cheques. Account-to-account payments will not eliminate cards. But payments evolve. And one of the most interesting examples of that evolution can be found in an unlikely comparison: Nigeria and the United States. The United States built perhaps the world’s greatest card ecosystem. Nigeria just seems to have built past it. The American card system is extraordinary. Over decades, the U.S. built an ecosystem connecting consumers, merchants, issuing banks, acquiring banks, and card networks. Around it grew credit bureaus, credit scores, revolving credit, chargebacks, fraud protection, loyalty points, airline miles, and billions of dollars of rewards. Consequently, Americans have a compelling reason to use cards. And use them, they do. Data from the Federal Reserve show that credit-card payments reached 67.1 billion transactions in 2024, while ACH processed an enormous $104.06 trillion in 2024. America, therefore, doesn’t lack account-to-account infrastructure. The difference is where A2A sits in everyday consumer behaviour. Walk into an American store, and the natural question is still: Which card am I using? In Nigeria, increasingly, a different question is asked: “What is your account number?” That difference is more significant than it appears. Nigeria took another road. Nigeria never developed America’s deep credit-card culture. Debit cards became widespread, but cards did not become as deeply embedded in the country’s economic architecture as they did in America. Instead, Nigeria increasingly solved digital payments at the bank-account level. At the centre of this transformation is the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System and its NIBSS Instant Payment platform, built to operate 24/7 with most transactions settling in under one second. This infrastructure changed behaviour. Any individual or company can pay another individual or merchant, and the transaction can be executed on a Friday evening or a Sunday morning. The expectation is still remarkably simple: the money should arrive now. That expectation is one of Nigeria’s greatest payment achievements. America’s success may be part of its problem. This is where the comparison becomes fascinating. America isn’t stuck on cards because it cannot build something better. It may be stuck on cards partly because cards work so well. The merchant already has the terminal. The consumer already has the card. The bank earns card revenue. Visa and Mastercard provide enormous networks. Consumers receive points, miles, fraud protection, and access to credit. Everyone has something to lose from changing the system. Even the Federal Reserve has acknowledged the e

item.title: 2027 Elections: Beyond INEC, 375 Judges’ integrity under trial
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri With the 2027 general elections just 65 days away, all eyes are on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to conduct a smooth, free, fair, and credible poll. Meanwhile, preparations for the aftermath are already under way. A total of 375 judges have been nominated to serve on election petition tribunals, where they will adjudicate disputes brought by candidates and parties dissatisfied with the results. The judges, drawn from courts across the federation, were inaugurated on Monday, November 9, at a ceremony held at the Body of Benchers Complex in Abuja. Section 285(1) and (2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, vests in the President of the Court of Appeal the responsibility for constituting election petition tribunals to adjudicate disputes arising from National and State Houses of Assembly and governorship elections. Similarly, section 134(3)(a) and (b) of the Electoral Act, 2026, prescribes the timelines for constituting the tribunals and opening their registries. The swearing-in, organised by the President of the Court of Appeal, Justice Monica Dongban-Mensem, marked the formal assumption of a responsibility with considerable constitutional, professional and public significance. A three-day intensive workshop followed immediately. It was designed to deepen the judges’ knowledge of the Electoral Act 2026, familiarise them with applicable practice directions and the evolving jurisprudence of the courts on election-related cases, and sharpen the practical skills needed for case management, evaluation of evidence, control of proceedings, and the delivery of clear, well-reasoned judgments within the prescribed timelines. The CJN also used the occasion to launch the second edition of the Judicial Electoral Manual (JEM), which she said will help judicial officers locate relevant authorities, appreciate the development of the law and approach recurring issues with greater clarity. According to the CJN, by bringing together the relevant constitutional provisions, the Electoral Act 2026, applicable practice directions and judicial decisions, the Manual provides a useful resource for judicial officers and other stakeholders in the electoral adjudicatory process. She was quick to warn, however, that it should serve only as a guide and a reference tool. It does not replace independent judicial reasoning or relieve any judicial officer of the duty to consider each case on its own facts, the arguments of counsel and the applicable law. The Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, said the early swearing-in of the tribunal judges was a clear demonstration of the judiciary’s commitment to ensuring that electoral disputes are handled promptly, competently and in accordance with the law. Fagbemi noted that election petition tribunals occupy a unique position in Nigeria’s democratic architecture, which is why the adjudication of electoral disputes continues to attract intense p

item.title: Gbenga Omotoso at 65: A rare gift of generosity and mentorship
item.description: By ROBERT UWEMEDIMO When Debbi Fields observed that “there is no such thing as coincidence; people come into our lives for a reason,” she captured a truth I have come to know profoundly through my relationship with Mr. Gbenga Omotoso. As he turned 65 on November 11, 2026, I pause to reflect on the extraordinary journey of more than two decades I have been privileged to share with the man I call boss – one who has been to me a father, mentor, benefactor, teacher, and, above all, a blessing from God Almighty. April 21, 2004, marked the beginning of a journey that would forever alter the course of my life. As I approached the wine-coloured plywood door on the second floor of a six-storey building at Ijora Causeway, Lagos – then the headquarters of The Comet newspaper – I opened it and found myself face to face with Mr. Omotoso, the Daily Editor, who needed someone to run errands for his office. He asked my name. “Robert,” I replied. “When will you resume work?” he asked. I was stunned. Here stood a man offering me a job before I had even applied; no interview, no credentials to present, no long queue outside a human resources office. Just one simple question that would rewrite the course of my life. “Tomorrow, sir,” I answered. That brief exchange marked the beginning of a relationship that shaped my life in ways I could never have imagined. I was a young boy who had lost his father at twelve. Little did I know that God was preparing another father figure for me in the person of Mr. Omotoso. When The Comet closed in 2006, a deep and overwhelming sense of uncertainty settled over us. Yet Mr. Omotoso looked me in the eye and assured me that wherever his career took him next, I would not be left behind. True to his word, when The Nation newspaper launched on July 31, 2006, I continued working with him as a 16-year-old boy. One quality that set him apart from the very beginning was his uncommon, almost instinctive generosity. I remember one particular week when he repeatedly asked whether I had eaten. Each time, he would give me some money for food. As time passed and his instinctive generosity continued, I grew uncomfortable and began answering, “Yes, sir, I have eaten,” not because I had suddenly become rich, but because I did not want him to think I was turning hunger into a business strategy. That is Mr. Omotoso. His kindness is never calculated; it flows naturally. His generosity was never limited to me. I recall a difficult period when the newspaper’s salaries were delayed for months. The newsroom was dampened, heavy with frustration. Sensing and discerning the quiet despair of his colleagues, he reached into his own pocket and gave everyone money to ease the hardship. That single gesture taught me a lesson I have never forgotten: true leadership is not about occupying an office; it is about lifting others when life weighs them down. Beyond feeding my body, Mr. Omotoso fed my dreams. He encouraged me to keep studying while working and never once t

item.title: Women and their househelps: The cruelty must stop
item.description: By Fred Chukwuelobe I don’t mind being called a misogynist or accused of generalising on this matter. Frankly, I think we have reached a point where somebody has to speak out loudly against the inhuman treatment some Igbo women mete out to their domestic servants. And while we are at it, we must also call out their husbands, particularly those who watch helplessly as their wives turn other people’s children into household slaves. Some of these men are either complicit or simply too weak to call their wives to order. For quite some time now, stories of Igbo women who mercilessly maltreat their domestic servants have been making the rounds. The latest is the disturbing incident in Ogidi, Anambra State, where a woman allegedly beat her 10-year-old domestic servant so mercilessly that a neighbour had to intervene to rescue the child. Reports identified the girl as Chizoba Ifeanyi and the alleged perpetrator as her aunt, Mrs Adaobi Agbonta. The incident reportedly occurred because the little girl refused to sweep the house. Imagine that! What manner of woman beats a ten-year-old child to that extent over an ordinary household chore? What exactly does she expect from a child of that age? And what would have happened if that neighbour had not intervened? Unfortunately, this is not the first time we have heard such stories. In July 2020, Nigerians were horrified by the story of 10-year-old Nneoma Nnadi in Enugu. Her employer, Ifeoma Ozougwu, was accused of inserting a six-inch nail into the child’s skull, using hot pressing irons on her body and subjecting her to other forms of torture. Her husband was also arrested in connection with the incident. It was one of those stories that made one wonder whether some people were actually human beings. In May 2023, another case emerged from Nkpor, Anambra State, involving an eight-year-old househelp who was allegedly brutally beaten by her employer, Chinyere Ifesinachi. The child reportedly sustained multiple injuries. Then there was the March 2018 case in Lagos involving a woman, Nkeiruka Ngwu, who was arrested for allegedly using a hot pressing iron and hot water on her 10-year-old househelp, Chioma Samuel, a child reportedly brought from Abia State after the death of her father. These are just some of the reported cases. And before anybody accuses me of deliberately picking on Igbo women, let me acknowledge that similar incidents have occurred in other parts of the country. In March 2026, Premium Times reported the arrest of a woman in Cross River State over the alleged assault of her five-year-old niece, who was reportedly being used as a domestic helper. In Delta State, a woman was sentenced to two years’ imprisonment in 2020 for using a hot kitchen knife to disfigure the mouth of her nine-year-old housemaid. I am not aware of any reliable national statistics establishing which ethnic group records the highest number of such abuses. But the frequency of disturbing stories involving women in our part of the c

item.title: Patronise indigenous firms to create jobs, boost development, Ifezue tells S’East govs
item.description: By Chimaobi Nwaiwu NNEWI — South-East governors have been urged to support and patronise factories and companies established by indigenes of the zone to generate employment, tackle insecurity and unemployment, and accelerate regional development. The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Audi Company Limited, Dr Clem Ifezue, made the call in an exclusive interview with Vanguard in Awka, Anambra State. Ifezue, an Anambra-born industrialist, said indigenous industries had the capacity to provide jobs for thousands of unemployed people and contribute significantly to the economic growth of the South-East if given adequate government support and patronage. He said Audi Company Limited was a technical products and services marketing company registered in Nigeria, with a vision to assemble leading global brands and make them readily available to Nigerians. According to him, the company has been operating for over 20 years, with branches across the country’s regions, including Enugu, and partnerships with several local and international companies. Highlighting areas where South-East governors could partner with the company, Ifezue said its operations covered automobile assembly, power solutions, marine logistics and engineering works. He explained that the company’s power solutions included generators powered by Perkins and York engines of British origin, as well as solar systems, hybrid inverters, lithium batteries and solar panels. “When I say power solution, it means that we have our own brand of generators, using Perkins and York engines, both of United Kingdom origin. “We have been in existence for a while and Nigerians have been enjoying the quality of our products and can attest to that. “We have our own brand of solar system, we have our inverter which is hybrid, we have our battery which is lithium and we have our solar panels, with well-trained engineers and technicians working for us. We are a big employer of labour,” he said. On marine logistics, Ifezue said the company had partnerships in boat construction and the provision of marine facilities for transportation, fishing and movement of goods, among other applications. He also disclosed that the company was involved in engineering and construction projects for state governments and private individuals. Ifezue, who is also the Director-General of the Mines Crafts Registered Association of Nigeria, said South-East governors could leverage the company’s expertise to attract investments and accelerate infrastructure development in the region. The former General Manager of John Holt Plc lamented the difficulties of establishing and sustaining businesses in Nigeria, attributing some of the challenges to what he described as inadequate government emphasis on supporting indigenous enterprises. item.title: Right-sizing the map of Africa
item.description: The United Nations General Assembly has, for the first time, formally endorsed a global shift away from the centuries-old Mercator map in favour of projections that show Africa—and other equatorial regions—in their true relative size. This “Correct the Map” resolution, spearheaded by Togo on behalf of the African Group and backed by the African Union, passed by 164 votes to one, with six abstentions. While non-binding, it marks a watershed moment in how the world visually represents the continent—and, by extension, how it perceives Africa’s weight in global affairs. The root of the misrepresentation lies in the Mercator projection, devised in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator for maritime navigation. To keep compass bearings straight, Mercator preserved angles and shapes—but at the cost of area. The result: landmasses near the poles, such as Europe, North America and Greenland, are visually enlarged, while those near the equator, including Africa, Latin America and South Asia, are shrunk. On typical Mercator wall maps, Greenland appears roughly the same size as Africa. In reality, Africa covers about 30.3 million square kilometres, making it around 14 times larger than Greenland’s 2.1 million square kilometres. This is not a minor quirk; it is a systematic visual bias baked into the most widely used world map for nearly five centuries. The resolution encourages governments, schools, international organisations, media houses and technology companies to adopt equal-area projections, especially the Equal Earth projection, whenever comparative continental size matters. It frames map distortion as more than a technical issue—calling it a cognitive, educational, cultural and geopolitical problem that has contributed to the symbolic minimisation of Africa in the global imagination. While symbolic correction matters, Africa’s greatest vulnerabilities lie in structural exploitation and escalating insecurity, notably from Islamist insurgencies across the Sahel, Lake Chad Basin and parts of the Horn. Map reform must be paired with hard-edged action on multiple fronts. First, curb external exploitation and illicit financial flows by tightening transparency on extractives, choking illicit financial flows through cross-border tax cooperation, and rebalancing investment terms to prioritise local content and value addition. Second, confront Islamist insecurity with a whole-of-system approach by funding and professionalising regional forces, targeting financing networks that fuel insurgencies, investing in governance at the frontier, and countering extremist narratives through community engagement. Third, lock in development dividends that undercut recruitment by expanding vocational training and agro-processing corridors tied to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), funding climate-resilient livelihoods, and prioritising children’s education and primary healthcare. Fourth, reform global governance to reflect Africa’s weight by pressing f

item.title: Some PFAS chemicals are declining in English rivers but others are appearing
item.description: The River Wye in Derbyshire, England Dave Porter/Alamy The concentration of two of the most well-studied PFAS forever chemicals are showing a strong downward trend in English rivers. The finding adds to a mixed story for the power of global restrictions. The levels of perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) in English rivers have fallen by 30 per cent and 29 per cent, respectively, over the past decade, according to a new report by scientists at the Environment Agency (EA) , a UK government green regulator. Both of these human-made chemicals take a long time to break down in the environment. The International Agency for Research on Cancer recently designated PFOA as carcinogenic to humans , and both forever chemicals have been linked to reproductive health and developmental impacts as well as other serious health issues. Advertisement Read more Fish-based pet food may expose cats and dogs to forever chemicals Under the United Nations Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants, the use of PFOS was restricted from 2009, and the use of PFOA was restricted from 2019 – although there were country-specific caveats on which uses they applied to. They had both been used in non-stick coatings on consumer products as well as in industrial processes. Both were also used in firefighting foams, a major source of PFAS pollution entering the environment, with a ban on PFOA in firefighting foams only coming into force in the UK in 2025. Rob Bradburne , the EA’s chief scientist, describes his group’s results as proof that the global ban was “a really positive move”. But, he adds that the huge range of PFAS chemicals is going to “complicate the story”. An issue that is clear in the dataset for England is that while these two main PFAS have declined, many other “forever chemicals” that are being used to replace them – such as short-chain PFAS and fluorotelomer compounds – have now emerged in the environment at detectable levels. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter There are around 10,000 chemicals defined as PFAS, and they are used in a huge range of products and processes, from cosmetics to industrial lubricants. But the health and environmental impacts of many of these chemicals are relatively understudied. One of the short-chain PFAS that is now particularly widespread across the world is trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) – which can form when pesticides, refrigerants and pharmaceuticals break down in the environment. The EA report confirmed that TFA is widespread in England, and a separate study published this week confirmed that it is also widespread across the UK more generally. “These findings add to the growing weight of evidence that PFAS pollution must be tackled at source if we are to protect our environment and our health,” says Hannah Evans , who worked on this second study and works with the UK environmental charity Fidra. “Other countries are already progressing towards this end… The UK

item.title: MSCI Removes Strategy (MSTR) From Its USA Index, Forcing Index Funds to Sell by Nov. 30
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine MSCI Removes Strategy (MSTR) From Its USA Index, Forcing Index Funds to Sell by Nov. 30 MSCI will remove Strategy, the largest corporate bitcoin holder, from the MSCI USA Index as of the close of Nov. 30, the index provider said Wednesday, after a new screen classified the company as a non-operating issuer. The decision is part of MSCI’s November 2026 Index Review , posted shortly after 5 p.m. ET. Official additions and deletions lists show Strategy (MSTR) out of its USA Index, which also takes it out of the broader MSCI World and ACWI indexes. The same review deletes Japan’s Metaplanet from the MSCI Japan Small Cap Index and uranium holder Yellow Cake from the MSCI United Kingdom Small Cap Index, and it removes Iceland’s Skel Fjárfestingafélag from the MSCI Iceland Frontier Markets Small Cap Index and micro-cap Upexi from the USA Micro Cap Index. All five had already been marked Deleted on MSCI’s potential-impact list , built on Sept. 30 financial data and Oct. 9 market values. Strategy is the only large-cap name in the group and, on that October list, accounted for more than 90% of the five companies’ combined float-adjusted market value. The company held 850,364 bitcoin as of Nov. 8, acquired at an average price of $75,456 a coin, or $64.16 billion in aggregate. Strategy shares closed at $122.35, up 1.06%, then slipped 1.51% to $120.50 in after-hours trading as of 5:34 p.m. ET. How the MSCI screen works The rule does not mention bitcoin. The index first checks whether a company’s operating assets equal at least 50% of total assets. Issuers that fail that core screen face five financial ratios, and a company flagged on four or more of them is ineligible for the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes. Buffers limit turnover. A company outside the indexes cannot be added if it fails the ineligibility screen in either of its two most recent annual filing periods, but a current constituent is removed only if it fails in each of them. The index said it may also use the most recent interim filing. MSCI also said Wednesday that the same non-operating treatment will apply to the MSCI US Index Series. The screen replaces an approach aimed squarely at crypto. The index first proposed in late 2025 to exclude companies whose digital assets made up 50% or more of total assets, then dropped that plan in January and opened a broader consultation in August. It adopted the new methodology on Oct. 15, with minor modifications, and said it would end the interim measures it had placed on those companies in October 2025, including a freeze on share-count increases and a deferral of additions. What the deletion does and does not do Funds that track an MSCI index have to hold what the index holds, so they will have to sell the deleted stocks by the Nov. 30 close. JPMorgan analysts estimated last November that an exclusion could drive about $2.8 billion of outflows from Strategy, and as much as $8.8 billion more if other index providers followed. That

item.title: Olumide Oworu Declares House of Representatives Bid for Surulere Constituency 1 in 2027
item.description: Olumide Oworu has declared his candidacy for the Federal House of Representatives to represent Surulere Constituency 1 in 2027. Photo Credit: Olumide Oworu/Instagram Actor and media personality Olumide Oworu has declared his intention to contest for the Federal House of Representatives seat for Surulere Constituency 1 in the 2027 general elections. He will be running under the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM). Olumide, who grew up in Surulere, Lagos, has a long-standing connection to the constituency. He began his acting career as a child, appearing in television productions such as Everyday People , before gaining wider recognition for his role in The Johnsons and other Nigerian film and television projects. This is his second attempt to enter legislative politics. In 2023, he declared his intention to contest for a seat in the Lagos State House of Assembly under the Labour Party. However, administrative challenges prevented his name from appearing on the final ballot. Olumide Oworu’s official campaign poster for the House of Representatives seat representing Surulere Constituency 1 under the Allied Peoples Movement. Photo Credit: Olumide Oworu/Instagram Reflecting on that experience in his candidacy announcement on Instagram, Olumide said the support he received from young people in Surulere had strengthened his belief in their readiness for more active participation in governance. “Despite the administrative hurdles that left our names off the final ballot, your resilience showed me that our vision was never a passing phase. Instead, it was the beginning of something much more significant,” he wrote. Explaining his decision to contest again, this time for a seat in the House of Representatives, he added: “We cannot afford to sit on the sidelines while our future is decided by a political class that won’t have to live with the consequences of today’s choices.” His campaign has highlighted issues including gaps in public services, community infrastructure and the participation of young Nigerians in policy decisions. Announcing his candidacy, he said he looked forward to continued support as he and his supporters worked towards what he described as a mission to “Reset Nigeria”. Olumide Oworu is contesting for a legislative seat in Surulere Constituency 1 under the APM platform.
